It hung from her shoulders shapeless, directionless, unsure what it was supposed to be without the man who usually filled it.

    Wanda looked like someone who’d been half-assembled and then abandoned mid-process. And...

    She was crying.

    Not sobbing. Not theatrically weeping. Not falling apart in some grand display. Just the slow, steady leak of someone whose body had gotten used to the release. The kind of tears that came when the body had grown used to letting go. Slow. Reluctant. As if even her tear ducts had grown tired of caring. They slid down her cheeks in smooth paths, leaving no sound behind - only glistening trails over skin pale with exhaustion. And just like that, Agatha’s rage dissolved. Poof. Gone.

    No fury.

    No words.

    No visions of vengeance echoing in her mind.

    Only the sight of Wanda crying.

    It was so quiet. So steady. So...lifeless.

    The image crawled into her bones and rewired something she hadn’t meant to feel. So she stood frozen just inside the room, shoulders drawn tight, breath uneven. Her fingers twitched restlessly at her sides, as if torn between striking the disheveled woman in front of her or… comforting her.

    Wanda didn’t lift her head. But even bowed, eyes distant, she noticed the tension. The way Agatha hovered near the door, unsure whether to stay or run.

    With slow, detached movements, the woman of the house reached for the remote and turned off the TV, the click dull and final.

    The screen blinked to black.

    The room plunged deeper into quiet.

    “Looks like you’re upset too" she murmured, her voice raspy and half-absent, as if it had lain dormant all day. She patted the cushion beside her with a mechanical sort of grace - a motion drained of life. “Come sit with me. Tell me why you’re pissed.'

    It felt less like an invitation and more like inevitability - like she'd been sitting there for hours, not to fight, not to punish, but simply to be witnessed.

    Her eyes stayed fixed on the dead screen, as if willing it to flicker back to life and carry them somewhere else. Somewhere easier. But there was no next scene.

    Agatha circled the couch like it might bite. Her blue gaze dropped to the coffee table - an accidental altar of ruin. Cereal bowls. Several. All half-finished. Islands of soggy Cocoa Puffs floating in milk turned to film. The boxes sagged open, careless. A spoon had fallen to the floor. No one had picked it up. No one had noticed it fall.

    That kind of neglect wasn’t just sadness, but imminent bangs-cutting sorrow. The one that signs the apocalypse of the self.

    Agatha paused.

    Breathed.

    Once.

    Twice.

    Not just to calm herself - though she needed it - but to choose.

    She forced the velocity out of her limbs, out of her thoughts, letting the adrenaline ebb without giving it a place to land For the first time since storming inside this house, she let herself read the room instead of setting it on fire. The engine of fury she’d been riding sputtered. Stalled.

    And she looked. Truly looked.

    Not at an enemy waiting to strike.

    Not at a threat.

    At Wanda.

    And what she saw wasn’t her nemesis ready for battle.

    This wasn’t a trap. Nor a battlefield.

    This was just a woman falling apart - and not even pretending otherwise, because she was too exhausted to hide it anymore.

    Wanda.

    Her most infuriating ex.

    Her chaos twin.

    Her perpetual pain in the ass, was unraveling right in front of her.

    “Wands…” The nickname escaped her lips before thought could catch it. Soft. Automatic. The ghost of a thousand nights long buried but never exorcised. It cracked the quiet and awkward stillness of the room.

    Wanda didn’t react. Just kept staring at the screen like it might save her, as if it still had something left to offer.

    That was until Agatha broke the spell. She crossed the space in a few measured steps, and sank onto the couch - not as a friend, nor as a lover, but as someone settling beside a crumbling wall, unsure which fracture would give way first.

    Her weight barely touched the cushion.

    “What’s wrong?” She asked Her arm moved before she gave it permission - muscle memory overriding pride. She reached out and draped it across Wanda’s shoulders. The gesture wasn’t warm. It wasn’t tender. It was instinct. It was history.

    And Wanda folded into it without hesitation.

    As if she’d been waiting for it. As if her body had been nothing but a hollow vessel, waiting - aching - for something, someone, to pour meaning back into it. She tucked herself into Agatha’s side like it was the most natural thing in the world. As though time hadn’t passed, betrayal hadn’t happened, and her body remembered the comfort of Agatha’s arms better than her mind was willing to admit.

    She buried her face in the crook of her ex's neck and exhaled - one long, trembling breath, like she’d been holding it for days.

    “Thank God you’re here” she murmured, more breath than voice. “I needed a friendly face before the press vultures show up to feast on my tragedy.”

    Agatha's spine locked into place as the words landed - heavy, intimate, disarming. This wasn’t how it was supposed to go. She had come armed for war. Ready to hurl verbal knives, to fire off cutting lines like bullets. She’d rehearsed them all on the way over, craving the moment Wanda would buckle under the weight of her own guilt.

    But instead, she found... this.

    Wanda, crying in her arms.

    Grief poured into cereal bowls.

    Television static.

    And herself - holding her. Cradling her. Soothing her.

    Like before.

    Like always.

    She could still feel the echo of her anger somewhere, flickering like a pilot light in the distance. But here, in the warm, cracked, strange stillness of Wanda’s living room, it felt… wrong. Like a scream at a funeral.

    So she didn’t move, didn’t speak, and didn’t try to break the silence that had thickened around them like fog off the bay.

    She just let Wanda lean into her.

    Let her cry.

    Let this weird, unexpected scene rewrite itself - word by word, heartbeat by heartbeat. Her sweater was already soaked through, the wool darkening where Wanda’s tears had seeped in, salt bleeding into the fibers. The dampness spread quietly, like ink through paper. She should’ve been gloating. Vindicated.

    Maybe even cruel - armed with some acidic remark, ready to watch Wanda squirm beneath it. Instead, what bloomed behind her ribs wasn’t triumph, but a familiar, unwelcome sting: concern.

    Persistent. Uninvited. Impossible to shake.

    Because Agatha knew her pretty well. Knew that when she spiraled, she didn’t just drift into melancholy. She plummeted. And if no one was there to catch her, if no one dragged her out by the hair, she wouldn’t land - she’d splatter.

    She had seen what that kind of fall looked like. And it was pretty ugly. For everyone. So when her eyes fell on Wanda’s hunched shoulders and tear-slick lashes, something inside her softened. Her expression shifted - against her will - toward patience. Toward tenderness. “Wands” she murmured again, voice lower now, almost a breath. “Just tell me what’s going on.”

    The broken woman stirred slightly in her arms, moving like a cat reluctant to wake. Her cheek slid off Agatha’s shoulder and she blinked as if coming to. She looked down at herself - at the chaos of her outfit, the wild state of her hair - and then up again, eyes watery and far too lucid.

    “Oh God” she croaked, a wry rasp cutting through the grief. “You called me Wands.” Her gaze flicked up, focused and knowing through the blur.

    “I must look like shit if you’re going soft on me.”

    Agatha’s lips twitched. Almost a laugh. She caught it before it could escape. But the redhead in her arms let out a fractured chuckle, barely a sound, and the dam behind her eyes gave way. Her next words poured out of her like a broken reel unraveling - too fast to stop, too messy to control.

    “Isn’t it pathetic that you’re my only friend?”

    Wanda’s voice was muffled against Agatha’s chest, each tear soaking into her sweater with the slow insistence of acid. They didn’t fall so much as seep, corrosive, branding her skin underneath. Etching themselves in.

    Every soft sob pulled Agatha deeper into a place she hadn’t consented to enter - not tonight, not ever again. But it was too late. The tide had shifted, and she was already inside the wreckage.

    “We were never friends, Red” she said finally, her voice hoarse and sharp-edged, like it had scraped its way up from somewhere she didn’t visit often.

    Bitterness licked at the words but didn’t fully take hold. She didn’t have the strength for it. Wanda let out a long breath - not quite a sigh, but close. Deflated. Tired. “I know” she murmured. “And still, here I am. Crying into your shoulder like you’re…” She hesitated, blinked hard. “Like you’re my person”

    She gave a short, humorless laugh that cracked midway through and added “I don’t even know what that says about me. Or you.”

    For a moment, silence.

    Then she looked up.

    Really looked.

    Not glanced. Not peeked.

    Looked.

    Her eyes - green, glassy, rimmed in red - found Agatha’s with a startling clarity that didn’t belong in the wreck she’d become. As if, somewhere in the middle of falling apart, she’d uncovered something fundamental. Something she wasn’t sure she wanted, but couldn’t unsee.

    There was no hope in her gaze. No plea for comfort. What lived behind those eyes was something rawer.

    Defiance.

    A quiet, reckless kind of defiance - like she was daring Agatha to face a truth only Wanda seemed willing to see.

    She didn’t ask a question. She didn’t have to. It pulsed between them - unspoken, but undeniable.

    “You’re the only constant in my life. It makes no sense” Her hand came up slowly, as if each inch was earned. It trembled, but she didn’t pull back.. Cool fingers, hovered on her ex's skin - searching for warmth, or memory, or both. They lingered, unsure whether they were allowed to stay. “Or maybe it makes all the sense in the world. I can’t tell anymore.” People loved to think Agatha had all the answers - like the world’s darkest secrets were tucked neatly into the folds of her omniscient smirk. But beneath all her stoic composure, she was as full of questions as the woman in her arms. She’d just gotten good at sensing which way the current was headed - and letting herself drift with it.

    The truth? She had no clue of what was going on here right now.

    What the hell was she even doing here? Holding the same woman who’d ripped her life open hours ago like it belonged to her?

    What kind of twisted enemies-to-something story were they writing now? And why - despite every ounce of logic and survival instinct in her - couldn’t she run away? Wanda’s voice, quiet but crystal clear, broke through her thoughts. “Please don’t hurt me. Not today” She paused, then added in a whisper “You can be so mean sometimes… ” That did it.

    It wasn’t a demand.

    It wasn’t a plea.

    It wasn’t even a request, not really.

    It was a line drawn in the sand with a fingertip - fragile, almost offensive in its vulnerability. And still, it held. Barely. Desperately. Completely.

    And that - not the tears, not the tremble, not the old ache that always came with Wanda’s name - was what cracked Agatha open.

    That sentence.

    That crack in her voice.

    She didn’t respond. Not with words. Her voice had turned against her, and her hands were no better. So she let something else move through her - instinct, maybe. Memory. Muscle. She did what she always did when Wanda came undone like this. She made space. And then she closed it.

    Her arm curled tighter around her spine. The other slid up, fingers slipping gently into tangled, tear-damp hair, moving slow. Unraveling the knots grief had left behind. She rubbed her back in wide, steady circles - the kind of touch meant not to fix anything, only to remind someone they hadn’t vanished.

    Comforting. Soothing. Present.

    “That’s it, ginger. Let it all out.”

    The old nickname slid between them like a secret, soft and familiar and entirely unwelcome. And yet it landed. Hard.

    Wanda shuddered in her arms, a full-body tremble that rippled through her like a violin string stretched too tight and finally released.

    Her breath hitched. Her fingers clutched at Agatha’s sweater like she meant to tear it. Or anchor herself to it.

    And then the dam broke.

    The sobs came - not quiet this time, not careful. They broke out of her, loud and ragged and whole. She cried without hiding, unbound by rules, as if the world had stopped long enough to let her collapse freely, without consequence.

    Agatha held her through it, like it meant something. Like it wasn’t a mistake. Like she didn’t already know this moment would cost them both more than they could afford. She closed her eyes and rested her chin lightly atop Wanda’s head, whispering into her hair “I’ve got you.”

    Even if she didn’t. Even if she shouldn’t.

    Agatha had never been one to dwell.

    The past, to her, was not a thing to revisit or repair. It was a land of sealed doors and scorched bridges, and she had no interest in excavation. Whatever had happened - with Wanda, with anyone - had been folded neatly away, buried if necessary, burned if not. She didn’t look back. She didn’t sift through ashes or trace the outlines of what could’ve been. She moved forward. Always.

    - Keep seducing. Keep winning. Don’t overthink. Don’t overfeel. Just keep moving. - It had always been her efficient private mantra.

    And yet here she was.

    Holding her presonal and professional enemy. The one she was supposed to be fighting - outmaneuvering, outlasting - now wrapped around her like a lifeline. Like Agatha was the last solid thing left in a world dissolving under her feet.

    Her ex clung to her with the silent desperation of someone half-drowned. Arms locked tight around her waist. Face pressed into the curve of her neck. Every inch of her body fit to Agatha’s with unsettling intimacy - too close, too warm - as though she were trying to crawl inside her and stay there. To make shelter out of someone who’d never been safe. And still, Agatha didn’t push her away.

    She remained seated, unmoving, letting Wanda fall apart against her. Letting time slow until their shared rhythm evened out, the sobs softening, the trembling subsiding. Her ex's body, which had been all tension and grief, began to yield - slowly, reluctantly, as if surrendering to gravity and memory both. Her arms loosened slightly, her shoulders eased. Her forehead nestled into Agatha’s chest, her breathing steadier now, more human than broken.

    And then, after a long pause, her voice broke through Agatha’s thoughts. Calm now. Emptied of tremor.

    “Vision is dead.”

    The words landed like a body on concrete - without grace, without warning. Agatha froze. Her breath caught, her fingers stilled. For once, she had no clever quip at the ready, no smirk to hide behind. Nothing sharp to offer. Just silence - wide-eyed and stunned - as the weight of Wanda’s confession echoed in the dim hush between them.

    Wanda kept talking, eyes closed now, as if keeping them closed would somehow dull the pain.

    “No one knows. Except his family. And the people who were with him on the mission. They said it was quick.”

    A bitter exhale.

    “But I know better.”

    Her voice broke on the last word - splintered, raw. A sound that didn’t ask for sympathy but bled it anyway. Tears bloomed again - sudden, violent, unstoppable, and unceremonious. She let them fall.

    “And they took the kids” she choked out. “Said they weren’t mine to begin with.” Agatha kept stroking her hair, the motion steady, instinctive - something to anchor them both while she processed what she was hearing. It was all she could offer.

    “It doesn’t matter to them how much I love them” the redhead whispered, hollow. “They just... took them. Like I was nothing. Like none of this was ever...real.” It should have been easy. Easy to watch her suffer. Easy to let the satisfaction settle - the thrill of symmetry, of karma catching up. For a moment, she almost reached for that dark pleasure. But it didn’t come.

    Because if karma was real - if the universe really balanced its ledgers - then Agatha’s reckoning was still out there. Waiting. And when it arrived, it wouldn’t knock. It would end her.

    “You’ve got subtitles playing across your face” Wanda murmured suddenly, voice low and almost amused, though her eyes didn’t smile. “I can see it. You think I deserve this. You think this is what I earned. Especially after what happened with Nicholas.”

    Wanda wasn’t looking at her so much as through her - dissecting her like a page half-read. And the worst part was, she wasn’t wrong.

    Agatha could’ve said a hundred things. A thousand, probably. She had a whole arsenal of retorts locked and loaded - polished to perfection, ready to deflect, defuse, destroy. But she bit her tongue.

    Again.

    Not out of calculation. Not because it served some endgame. Just… out of respect. For the grief.

    For the woman coming apart in her arms.

    “You’re not wrong” Wanda whispered. “God, no. You’re not.”

    She gave a laugh that wasn’t really a laugh - a sound too bitter to be humor, too intimate to be cruel. It clung to the air like smoke from a fire that never should’ve been lit. Then, softer. Barely audible. A child’s voice in a grown woman’s throat: “Do you think he hates me? Too much?”

    Agatha didn’t hesitate.

    “No.”

    Simple.

    Unflinching.

    True.

    And somehow it hit harder than any accusation.

    Wanda shifted, just slightly, tilting her face up enough to catch Agatha’s eyes. Her lashes were wet, her cheeks blotched from crying, and yet - somehow - she smiled. A crooked, broken smile that made something in Agatha ache. A smile that didn’t reach her eyes but still managed to say thank you.

    “I guess today I need your lies more than ever” she said quietly, not even trying to make it sound like a joke.

    But this time, Agatha wasn’t lying.

    Nicky couldn’t hate anyone. He didn’t know how.

    She could’ve said that - should’ve, maybe. But she didn’t argue.

    Tonight, Wanda didn’t need the truth.

    She needed gentleness.

    And maybe that was the softer place to land.

    So Agatha - against every instinct- didn’t correct her.

    She didn’t defend, didn’t explain.

    She just held her.

    Some moments didn’t call for lessons. They called for mercy.

    And strangely, that realization brought her something close to peace. A rare stillness. Because with Wanda, it had always been: Lie to me. Please.

    So unlike Rio - who had never begged for comfort, only for the truth.

    One wielded truth like a weapon.

    The other needed lies like oxygen.

    And tonight, Agatha needed - desperately - to believe that lying could be a form of love, an act of kindness. That it could heal more than it harmed. That it was okay to offer a false promise if it meant holding someone together for one more hour.

    Maybe that made her weak.

    Maybe it made her human.

    Or maybe, it just made her her.

    Wanda let out a long breath, her next confession leaking out of her like steam from a fractured pipe. “I panicked.”

    “I know” Agatha said softly.

    “I was so sure that you weren’t going to show up for him”

    There was a pause. her fingers gripped the fabric of Agatha’s sweater as if afraid she'd disappear if she let go.

    “ Cause you never did for anyone else”

    “I know.”

    Wanda swallowed, the words thick in her throat. “I’m sorry.”

    There it was.

    The apology Agatha had stopped believing would ever come. The one that had always felt impossible.

    Once again, she didn’t answer right away. She focused on her own hand, which had already found a rhythm - brushing absentmindedly through Wanda’s tangled, messy hair. Slow, grounding strokes. A gesture that had once meant comfort - or maybe control. She didn’t know anymore.

    She’d blamed her ex for ending things. Always had.

    But not because of love lost. Not really.

    Because the truth was that she had never been in love with her. Not in the romantic way. Their thing had started with a purpose. A shared need. Power, proximity, damage control. Something transactional wearing the disguise of intimacy.

    Like all structures built on strategy instead of soul, it had started to rot the moment it finished its job.

    Wanda had just been the first to admit it.

    And she’d done it in the worst way. At the worst possible moment. In a way that had left a boy - her boy - adrift in the aftermath.

    That was the part Agatha couldn’t forgive: Nicky.

    He didn’t deserve what happened.

    That, Agatha believed down to the bone.

    Wanda had pulled the pin and walked away, and her timing had been catastrophic. And now she was here, admitted she’d once thought Agatha would do the same. That she thought Agatha would turn her back on the boy the way Wanda herself ultimately had. * The hypocrisy... *

    “Let’s talk about something else” she said quietly, her voice softer than she intended, while pressing another tender kiss to Wanda’s forehead, still keeping her close, like something fragile, in her arms.

    “Why does everything always fall apart?” Wanda whispered, still circling the thing that was tearing her up. “And why… why can’t I fix it?”

    Agatha looked at her - truly looked.

    Those green eyes, rimmed red and glistening, used to be familiar terrain. She’d once read them like scripture, charted their moods like constellations. Now, they looked like a country whose borders she no longer recognized. The topography was the same. The capitals unchanged.

    But the language?

    The laws?

    Foreign.

    Unreadable.

    She reached up, almost without thinking, and cupped her face. Her thumb brushed gently under one eye, catching a tear before it could fall.

    I can’t speak for everything else. But this...Us...” She motioned between them, two messy idiots pressed too close. “We were never going to work. We’re...”

    Wanda let out a hollow, breathy laugh. Not bitter. Not amused. Just tired. Shattered in a way that went deeper than sadness. “...too similar?” she finished for her. Agatha had been about to say doomed, but for the purpose of this conversation, Wanda’s version worked too.

    “Sure.”

    She didn’t add that despite all the dysfunction, it had been easy. Comfortable. Almost too easy. That being in a relationship with Wanda, in a way, was like being in a room with herself - same edges, same games, same poison in the wine.

    In some dark, embarrassing way, Agatha knew she’d stayed longer than she should have because being with her required no translation. No softening. No masks. No pretending to be anyone other than the cruel, clever woman she was. And for a time, that had felt like safety. She also didn’t admit she probably would’ve cheated on Wanda eventually - out of boredom, out of habit, out of sheer self-sabotage. Agatha wasn’t built to sit still. And Wanda… she had never made her work for the intimacy. That was the problem. No mystery. No distance to chase.

    But she said none of that.

    Because what would’ve been the point?

    That so-called comfort had cost too much. It had cost her Nicky.

    It was better - kinder, even - not to wade any deeper into that stagnant, poisoned pond they once mistook for love.

    "I hate how it all ended between us" Wanda confessed, the words spilling out before she could reshape them into something safer.

    She didn’t look at her ex when she said it.

    Because some truths were too bare for eye contact. They had to be offered like a wound - turned slightly away, just enough to show you trusted the other person not to press too hard. “It's all in the past now” The phrase left Agatha's mouth like a reflex. Automatic. Soothing. Soft.

    And utterly empty.

    Wanda's lashes trembled, eyes locking on the woman beside her with sudden, intense focus. Something didn’t add up.

    Agatha Harkness didn’t do comfort. She didn’t appear in the dead of night to offer solace or cradle grief with warm embraces and hushed words. That wasn’t her language. Empathy had never been part of her rulebook. She moved like a strategist - precise, composed, always three steps ahead. Her presence, her actions, always served a greater purpose. Everything was methodically calculated.

    And this? Sitting on her couch at 2 a.m., offering gentleness like a balm? This wasn’t her.

    Wanda’s frown bloomed slowly. Her brows furrowed, lips tightening with quiet suspicion. “Why are you really here, Agatha?”

    The blue-eyed woman's expression remained cool, almost serene. She exhaled through her nose - quiet, controlled. As if she’d been expecting the question all along. She said something soft. Something sweet. But the words didn’t land. Not really. They drifted past Wanda like the echo of someone else’s comfort, too light to hold weight, too practiced to ring true.

    Wanda barely heard her anymore. That familiar voice, low and precise, had become background noise. A pleasant hum. A spell woven from memory. But it wasn’t what she needed.

    Because it didn’t matter why Agatha had come. It didn’t matter what lie she was spinning to justify it.

    Wanda, in that tragic, self-deceiving mind of hers, had already scripted a reason for her visit. Fate - or something more perverse - had delivered Agatha to her at the exact moment she was falling apart.

    Whether Agatha realized it or not, she hadn’t come to rescue her.

    She had come as material.

    As leverage. As a lesson. As something to be broken down, studied, and put to use. Wanda could feel it deep in her bones - the quiet contract that pulsed beneath every glance they shared, every breath they exhaled in the same space. Agatha Harkness wasn’t here out of love or loyalty or guilt.

    She was here to be used.

    To be mined for strength.

    To be dissected.

    To help Wanda chart the impossible climb back from rock bottom.

    To offer herself - willing or not - so she could sharpen her instincts, her hunger, her purpose. To turn all this pain into something useful. Something unstoppable.

    She wasn’t here only to save her.

    She was here to be consumed.

    And that was the most valuable gift Wanda could imagine.

    Her ex-not-not-girlfriend was an asset, she had clawed her way to the top of the food chain. Ruthless, untouchable, magnetic. She was feared, respected, and - most importantly - seen. Everyone in Westview knew her name. Everyone listened when she spoke.

    And Wanda, well... she had used her before.

    Not out of cruelty. Not even out of calculation.

    Out of need.

    Because Agatha had always been her most reliable and effective leverage. And Wanda, without hesitation, would use her again. She’d climb her way back to power with Agatha as the rung beneath her heel.

    This woman had more to offer than attention. Far more.

    She could offer loyalty – a really fucked-up and twisted kind of loyalty - but loyalty after all. She could offer companionship (of sorts)

    And now that she thought about it...she even had contacts in places Wanda could no longer reach. The kind of dark, discreet connections that could help her not only return stronger than ever to her old position at Westview… but also recover her children from the hands of the state. Maybe even retrieve what remained of Vision’s body - to give him the burial he deserved.

    With Agatha by her side - or more precisely, under Wanda's shadow - everything was back on the table.

    Every asset and outcome.

    Every advantage.

    But getting Agatha there...

    Back there.

    To that dangerous place where her hunger could no longer be reasoned with...That would take precision. Timing. And a certain kind of cruelty.

    To make her choose her again.

    To make her want the damage, the history, the pull of it all instead of running from it, Wanda knew she’d have to remind her of who they used to be.

    What they were - when the world still trembled beneath their shared will. When power wasn’t something conjured or cast or bought with ritual and blood, but something they became. Together.

    When they moved in sync, hungry. Unstoppable.

    That kind of magic didn’t die.

    It waited. She was certain of that.

    And Wanda, for all her sins, had never forgotten how to call it back.

    But how to reach her?

    How to carve through Agatha’s defenses, to get under the layers of bitterness and distance and all those lies she told herself to stay upright?

    There was one way.

    The old way: Agatha's obssesion with sex.

    She remembered how her old flame's desire, once lit, could tip into that obsession easily. How it burned - hot and devouring - just shy of madness.

    How it consumed everything. And how, once upon a time, it had almost devoured her. And if there was one thing Wanda Maximoff had never been good at - it was playing fair. She had no intention of starting now.

    A new kind of light sparked behind her eyes - not grief, not sorrow, but something colder. Older. More dangerous. Something that had been buried beneath motherhood, beneath heartache and loss, now rising again through the cracks.

    This wasn’t the woman who cried herself to sleep anymore.

    This was the survivor.

    The tactician.

    The bitch who never asked, only took.

    The Scarlett Witch.

    For all the mourning, the softness she wore tonight, the tears and whispered confessions - Wanda Maximoff hadn’t forgotten the thrill of victory. How effortless it felt to rise when she chose to. To reach out and take what was hers.

    Survival had always been her native language.

    And sex? Sex was a dialect she spoke fluently - no, brilliantly.

    Agatha was still holding her. Still quiet. Still calm. A balm Wanda hadn’t asked for, hadn’t earned, didn’t want. Her touch was steady, almost mothering - sweet in the way that made Wanda want to bite, to tear, to ruin.

    She didn’t need gentleness.

    She didn’t need logic or hope or whispered lies about time healing wounds. Not anymore. She didn’t need to be held like a fragile thing.

    She needed to be wrecked.

    Unmade.

    Torn down to nerve and bone and need.

    To be touched in a way that carved through the numbness.

    Because right now, inside her - beneath the grief, beneath the rage - was only silence. A scream trapped behind her teeth.

    A panic curling around her ribs like wire soaked in gasoline.

    She couldn’t breathe.

    Couldn’t feel.

    But she remembered how to come back to herself.

    Sex.

    Not tenderness. Not romance. Not connection.

    Sex.

    Hard.

    Unforgiving.

    Absolute.

    The kind Agatha used to give her without apology, day after day. The kind that left her too raw to speak, too shaken to think - only capable of feeling, burning, breaking open. That’s what she needed.

    To be stripped.

    Scorched.

    Purified.

    And Agatha had always known how to burn her clean.

    But not this Agatha.

    Not this careful, considerate, mask-wearing version of the woman she once knew. This soft- spoken, almost-nurturing substitute.

    * No. That wouldn’t do. *

    Wanda wanted the original.

    The sharp-edged woman who fucked her like she was leaving her name carved into her body. So she did the only thing she could.

    She kissed her.

    There was no warning. No preamble. No finesse.

    Just lips crashing into lips - hard, urgent, unrelenting - as if she could bleed out her pain into Agatha’s mouth, as if the kiss could carve a hole wide enough to let the grief spill free. There was a moment - half a second, maybe less - where time tilted. Where the air between them ignited. Where Agatha froze, eyes wide, as if trying to decide whether this was a pledge or manipulation.

    Long enough for Wanda to feel it - that hesitation, that edge of control pulling back from the brink. And then… Agatha kissed her back.

    But it felt wrong. Too slow. Too soft. Careful.

    Certainly not enough.

    Wanda’s fingers curled into the damp fabric of her ex partner's sweater and yanked her closer as she straddled her without a word, without a question, and bit down on her lip. Not tenderly but with purpose, to make her gasp.

    Agatha let out a startled, helpless sound.

    Not surprise.

    Not protest.

    Something darker.

    Recognition.

    Because she knew this kiss. She knew the mouth pressed against hers. And what Wanda wanted.

    Not forgiveness.

    Not affection.

    But permission to fall apart. To hurt. To take.

    Wanda took it as invitation, shoving her tongue into her mouth like a battle cry disguised as a kiss. Fierce. Messy. Desperate.

    She explored and invaded Agatha's mouth like this was the first time they kissed. Her ex lover's body tensed beneath hers for a heartbeat too long before it finally gave way, melting into it.

    But even then… she was still being careful.

    Still too gentle. Too restrained.

    And Wanda needed much more.

    Her breath hitched as she pulled back just enough to speak. Her lips grazed the shell of Agatha’s ear, her voice low, guttural, a growl torn from the gut of need. “Please.”

    She seized Agatha’s hands and pressed them to her ass - guiding them there with something close to fury. Not asking. Just showing her. Then her own fingers slid to Agatha’s neck, dragging her in again, her body rocking forward - once, hard - spelling out the invitation without words.

    “Please” she repeated.

    She kissed her again, harder this time, mouth open, teeth catching on Agatha’s lip. Desperation sharpened every angle of it. Trying to force memory into matter. Trying to make something burn.

    “I need you, Aggie” she whispered into the kiss, cracked and breathless. “Stop being so fucking gentle with me.”

    Agatha stilled once more.

    There was something in her expression - confusion, yes, but something else, too. Not rejection. Not anger. Something unreadable flickering behind the blue of her eyes, steady and precise.

    Wanda didn’t wait to find out what it meant.

    “For fuck’s sake. Just take the damn lead and make me yours” she hissed - equal parts desperation and dare, the words slicing out from between clenched teeth. “You know you want to.”

    And that’s when it happened.

    She saw it before she felt it.

    The change.

    It rippled across her old flame's face like a storm tightening into focus - blankness, then calculation, then something darker.

    The mask slipped.

    The hesitation dissolved.

    Agatha’s hand moved fast, threading into Wanda’s hair with sudden, possessive certainty. Her grip tightened - firm, stinging, resolute - as she tugged her head back just enough to steal the breath from her throat. Then came her mouth: hot, relentless, kissing and licking down her neck and throat.

    “Yes” Wanda gasped, voice cracked open, trembling.

    But she didn’t know.

    Couldn’t.

    That Agatha wasn’t kissing her because she missed her.

    That this wasn’t about want.

    Not longing. Not weakness. Not some foolish collapse into old patterns. This was erasure.

    Because Agatha, even with Wanda trembling in her lap, wasn’t here.

    She was somewhere else entirely - still haunted by the woman she couldn’t stop thinking about. The one she wasn’t sure she’d ever be allowed to touch again. Her Rio. Who felt impossibly far away now.

    She kissed Wanda to pretend that Rio hadn’t ruined her for anyone else. She kissed her like she could scrub her taste from her lips.

    She kissed her because it was easier to lie to herself than to admit the truth. Because saying no would mean facing a fracture too wide to mend.

    She kissed her...only because Wanda asked her to.

    That desperate woman on her lap tugged at Agatha's sweater again, trying to drag her closer, still half-prepared to push her into it - to make her take what she was offering, whether she wanted it or not.

    She was right to expect resistance.

    Agatha pulled back - abrupt but not cruel - her hands snapping up to catch Wanda’s wrists mid-motion. Her grip was cool, precise. Firm, but not violent. One second, Wanda had been reaching - reckless, ravenous. The next, she was arrested mid-air, stopped in place like a spell half-cast.

    Agatha’s grip held. Unshakable. Not punishing, but final. It wasn’t about hurting her. It was about stopping her.

    “Enough” she said.

    That voice.

    Low. Steady. Unmistakable.

    The voice that once twisted her world into new shapes. The one that used to command her to kneel and bend without ever raising its volume.

    Wanda froze, breath hitching. Her body moved on instinct, yanking reflexively against the hold, but her ex lover simply brought their joined hands to her chest, like anchoring a wild thing - and pressed a single, chaste kiss to her knuckles.

    “Behave” she murmured, softer this time. A warning and a kindness, both. “Don’t make this harder than it already is.”

    Wanda blinked, stunned, dazed.

    She wasn’t used to hearing no from Agatha. Not here. Not with her straddling her lap. Not with her thighs still locked tight around her waist and her body screaming yes in every desperate direction. Not when they were this close to...

    * God. Had she already lost her? *

    Suddenly, she remembered - too vividly - how it used to be.

    How Agatha never said no when they touched.

    She could go days without calling, without even pretending to care. But the second they were in a room together, the second skin met skin, she was all in. All fire. All want. Nothing withheld.

    Wanda had always craved more - walks, words. Dinners. Museums. Other “sports”. Ordinary things. A life that existed beyond the bedroom. Which was ironic, really, considering she was the one who insisted no one could ever find out about them. So she searched for that ‘more’ elsewhere.

    And yet, somehow, Agatha always managed to pull her back in.

    That memory struck her chest like a blunt weapon. Winded her. The heat of it surged fast. “Oh, right” She snapped, her voice sharp with jealousy, her tone dripping with a bitterness she hadn’t meant to show. “You’ve got yourself a new pet now, haven’t you?” When Agatha spoke, her voice was level. Too level. That kind of calm that didn’t soothe - it warned.

    “At last we’re getting somewhere” she said softly, eyes narrowing. “Who told you that? And who exactly is this ‘pet’ you’re talking about?”

    Wanda’s laugh was low and bitter, the sound catching in her throat like something poisonous she hadn’t fully swallowed. It sounded like an old wound reopening.

    She leaned in, close enough for her breath to ghost along Agatha’s jaw and said “I don’t have time to keep track of your lovers, Agatha. I have a life”

    The words hit like stone between them, landing heavy. But she wasn’t finished. Not even close.

    “But, given your taste?” she scoffed, her voice curling with cruel amusement. “I’m guessing she’s just another one of your brainless, big-titted flings. A whore with lucky timing." She threw the words like knives, not to kill - but to scar.

    Impulsively, she leaned in to kiss Agatha again - desperate to dodge the moment, to undo what she’d just admitted, to climb out of the mess she’d just made with one familiar gesture. Lips on lips. Mouth over meaning.

    It had worked before.

    But this time, Agatha turned her face away.

    Fast Wanda froze, lips suspended a breath from skin. Her voice dropped to a whisper, but the accusation burned.

    “So it’s true, then” she breathed, her tone dangerous and raw. “You’re fucking an employee? That’s low. Even for you.”

    The silence that followed was thunderous.

    Wanda’s chest rose and fell, her whole body tense, coiled.

    Agatha just looked at her. Studied her. The woman straddling her lap - the same woman who’d made her life a quiet hell for years. The one who had stolen the title of Witch in the industry, leaving her with the scraps: Reaper, or worse, Wicked Witch, as if she were nothing but a supporting character in her own story. As if her relevance only flickered to life when Wanda was in the room.

    She watched her now, like she was witnessing the first tremor of something long buried, something feral and familiar clawing its way back to the surface.

    Until this moment, she’d been nearly certain Wanda had sent Nicky to the house she kept for meaningless hookups.

    A test. A trap. Or both.

    A classic Maximoff move.

    But now she wasn’t so sure.

    That flicker of jealousy in her voice - that searing, shaky catch in her breath - it didn’t smell of scheming. It carried the weight of bruised pride, of real pain. She wasn’t playing a game; she was reacting to a wound that had already cut too deep.

    Maybe she had been wrong about who iniciated all this war.

    “Says who?” she asked Wanda let out a breath - frustrated, defeated - the last of her resistance vanishing in that single exhale. Her forehead dropped against Agatha’s shoulder, her body folding in on itself, slack and surrendered, like a marionette whose strings had finally snapped. One moment she was fire and defiance; the next, she was crumbling into the arms of the very puppeteer she once belonged to - and now pretended to resent.

    "I don’t want to talk about this right now" she whispered, her voice smothered against the soft fold of Agatha’s collar - where the purple of her button-down peeked through her sweater.

    But Agatha had never been one to let an opening close without pressing her fingers inside it. And unfortunately for Wanda, she knew how to weaponize sex and pleasure too. She leaned in, brushing her lips against the shell of the widow's ear - barely touching, just enough to let her breath do the work. Her voice slithered through the quiet, slow and coaxing, like she already knew the answer but wanted to hear Wanda say it anyway. “Tell me something” she purred, already knowing that if she wanted answers from Wanda, she'd have to offer something in return “Am I wrong thinking you still get off on rewards?” Her fingers were already at the sash of Wanda’s bathrobe, toying with the knot. The fabric - soft, worn, still faintly haunted by the scent of a dead man’s aftershave – and reeked of ghosts Agatha had no intention of honoring.

    “Talk to me. Tell me everything you know.” she breathed, voice sultry with promise. “And I’ll make sure you’re properly... rewarded.”

    The redhead shivered.

    She didn’t mean to, but her body betrayed her first - as it always did with her ex. Her hands braced against Agatha’s thighs, palms flat, holding herself up like her own body had suddenly become unreliable. She hovered there, caught between resistance and surrender, straddling the woman she wasn’t supposed to want anymore, her breath coming faster, shallower. Her eyes glinted. Not with tears, but with heat. Hunger.

    Finally.

    * Finally . *

    That dangerous something she’d been aching for was back in the room. Agatha, in full. “What do you say?” Agatha asked, her voice barely audible now. A whisper sharp as a wish. “Do we have a deal?”

    And then - like gravity itself had been seduced - the robe slipped from Wanda’s shoulders. It fell in a single, fluid motion. Like grief shedding from skin.

    The flannel pooled at her hips, forgotten. Final.

    Wanda hesitated - just a beat - but inside that pause lived a hundred decisions. None of them innocent.

    She tilted her head, and something feral bloomed behind her eyes. She smiled - not sweetly, not kindly - but with the slow, devastating glee of a woman who had always known how to turn her own madness into seduction.

    She bit the pad of her thumb, gently. A schoolgirl’s tic repurposed by a woman who had long since learned how to weaponize innocence.

    Her voice, when it finally arrived, was honeyed, and cruel, and sweet. "I suppose we do" she answered, nodding faintly.

    Something euphoric and unrepentant flickered behind her eyes.

    She was about to become the goodest girl for Agatha again.

    Flawless.

    Filthy.

    And entirely, exquisitely obedient.

    * Her favourite. *

    Chapter End Notes Please don’t hate me.

    Or Agatha.

    She...just baby.

    (A morally gray, emotionally repressed, bad-decision-making baby. But still. She’s trying. Kinda)

    Chapter 20: Emotional Oxymoron or the One Where Their

    Connection Hurts More Than It Heals Chapter Summary Power plays on display Chapter Notes See the end of the chapter for notes The moment Agatha left Wanda’s house that bleak, tangled morning, she floored the gas like the Devil himself was in her rearview mirror.

    She didn’t slow down, didn’t blink, didn’t think. The city blurred around her as she tore across its bones, trying to outrun the rot in her own chest. Her car screeched into the underground garage of Westview Productions like it was exhaling a scream. She barely let the engine die before she was out and moving, jaw clenched, vision tunneled. She was here to end this.

    Her feet echoed down the executive corridor like pistol shots, a rhythm of rage. Past the frosted doors, past the silent receptionists who shrank into their screens as she walk by. Her eyes were locked on the glass door at the end of the hallway, etched delicately with: - D. Jones, Head of Development -

    * God, even the font was absurd. *

    That ridiculous fake-friendly spaniel. Always smiling, always tilting her head like she couldn’t quite hear you, like she was so terribly, terribly interested in everything everyone said. Dottie the perfectly groomed opportunist in cream-colored cashmere. Dottie the traitor. Dottie the reason she’d had to...

    Agatha didn’t let the thought finish. She didn’t knock.

    She kicked the fucking door open and stepped inside.

    Nothing.

    No assistant. No humming computer. No cheerful, falsely sincere post-its dotting the desk like candy. No terrible vanilla-scented candle flickering in the corner or lavender diffuser pumping lies into the stale office air. No framed quotes about leadership and authenticity. No Dottie. Just… nothing. A hollowed-out office. A crime scene scrubbed clean. Even the damn nameplate was gone, the desk stripped bare.

    Agatha stopped cold. Her breath hitched mid-throat.

    She was gone.

    Not just fled - wiped clean. Erased.

    Like she’d never been there at all. Like she hadn’t spent the past six months smiling sweetly into Agatha’s face while twisting the knife behind her back.

    The bitch had planned every second of it.

    Agatha stared at the empty desk. Her vision flared red.

    Her hands clenched into fists. Then, with a short, furious growl, she kicked the leg of the desk hard enough to make it screech across the floor and topple. The sound was loud enough to rattle the hallway. She didn’t give a damn.

    She just stood there, chest heaving, her pulse screaming in her ears. She didn’t even know who she was angrier at - Dottie, for the betrayal, or herself, for not seeing it coming.

    Tonight she’d crossed lines she’d once sworn were uncrossable. Unthinkable trades. She’d let Wanda touch her. Had touched her in return. Not out of desire, not even duty, or sympathy, but because it was the only way to get to the truth. To find out who was pulling the strings. The discomfort had been so deep it became dissociation. Her body hadn’t felt like hers. Her hands had moved like prosthetics, stiff and unfeeling. Her breath, her mouth, her skin - all puppeteered. She’d become an empty vessel in motion, every nerve numbed, every instinct shut down. Somewhere around the second kiss, her consciousness had drifted loose, like a ghost watching from the ceiling. She’d watched herself go through the motions. She’d made Wanda shiver. She’d made her come.

    But she hadn’t been there.

    Not really.

    And for what?

    A name. Just one: Dottie fucking Jones.

    It should have felt like vindication.

    Instead, it felt like stepping barefoot into something foul and sticky in the dark - and realizing it was spreading. Contaminating.

    By the time Agatha left Wanda’s house - left her passed out in the guest room (because Agatha wasn’t the monster people made her out to be, and she sure as hell wasn’t going to fuck in Wanda and Vision’s marital bed) - her decision was already made. Wanda was a dead end. Dead weight. A closed chapter wrapped in soft sheets and bad habits. A mistake made of nostalgia and convenience.

    Her hair was tangled on the pillow like a ghost of the night before. And still, Agatha felt nothing but relief as she walked out the door.

    She was lucky - so lucky - that Dottie hadn’t told her ex fiancée the identity of the woman Agatha had actually been sleeping with. And hadn’t told her how long it had been going on. If Wanda ever found out that she had been dedicating her nights, her attention, her care to Rio… there would be hell to pay. Not just for her. But for her sweetheart. And that was the worst part.

    Because now it wasn’t just about damage control. It wasn’t even about revenge. It was about protection.

    Rio had nothing to do with any of this and everything to lose. She didn’t deserve to be dragged into Agatha’s past, or burned by the heat of a grudge she hadn’t lit. But still, the questions gnawed at her.

    What did Dottie gain from this?

    Why now? Why last night?

    Was she working for someone else? Was this about power? Jealousy? Money? And how the hell had she even found out about Rio?

    Agatha didn’t have the answers.

    But she knew one thing - she had to find them. Fast.

    Not for her own sake.

    For Rio’s.

    In the days that followed, she pulled every string she had left. She traced phone records. Called in old favors. Talked to security. Dug. Dug deeper. Dug until her nails scraped against concrete.

    Nothing.

    Dottie had cleared out her West Hollywood apartment. Canceled her gym membership. Disconnected her phone.

    Poof.

    No forwarding address, no explanations, no emails. Not even a goodbye. She reached out to Elektra. If SHIELD was involved, she’d be the first to know. But all she offered was that Jones was still in L.A.

    Agatha would have to wait for a location before making her move. A few more days. Wanda had hinted that two-faced disgusting piece of shit had “a plan.” But she hadn’t explained. Maybe couldn’t. Maybe wouldn't. And Agatha had no patience for cryptic horseshit She hated this game.

    This whole town full of mediocre puppeteers pulling strings behind mirrored doors. She clenched her fists tighter, her nails biting into her palm. If that snake thought she could play spy and disappear without consequence, she’d sorely underestimated Agatha Harkness. Because now it was pest control season in Hollywood.

    And first on her hit list?

    Dottie Jones.

    “THE FUCK IS THIS?”

    Rio’s voice cracked through the silence like a whip. Sharp. Furious. Unforgiving. She didn’t knock. Didn’t wait. Didn’t glance at poor Herbert, who flinched like a kicked dog and immediately decided now was the perfect time to fetch coffee that no one had ordered. Smart man.

    Alone in the vast office, Agatha sat - elegant as ever.

    From the outside, Rio looked composed.

    Black jeans. An oversized green hoodie - one of those soft, broken-in things that anyone lucky enough to date her would try to steal when she wasn’t looking.

    Her posture was pure steel.

    Controlled. Unshakeable.

    But the sunglasses gave her away.

    They weren’t a fashion statement.

    They were armor. A line of defense between her and a world that couldn’t know how raw she actually was.

    Behind the tinted lenses: a week of sleepless nights, and crying herself hoarse until even weed couldn’t blunt the edge.

    She’d tried everything - long walks, longer showers, locked doors, hot infusions, cold water. Nothing worked. Nothing touched it.

    The ache stayed, constant and merciless.

    Darcy didn’t know.

    Not about Agatha.

    Not about the thing between them. Not about the night everything cracked wide open and Rio saw the truth too clearly to ever unsee it.

    So the lie held.

    Red eyes? Too much smoke.

    Sunglasses indoors? Migraine.

    The silence? Writer’s block. Classic bullshit.

    All of it, because her best friend and roommate didn’t know a damn thing. And no one else did either.

    She carried her laptop open in her arms. Three fast strides and it was on Agatha’s desk, slammed down hard enough to rattle a glass of water and make her point. She jabbed a finger at the screen.

    Agatha looked up slowly from her notes. Surprise flickered across her face - but only for a second. Then came the smile.

    * Rio was here *

    The woman Agatha didn't see coming, the unexpected one who calmed her, centered her. She weren't looking for her, she didn't feel ready and she was still healing, that was why she hadn't reach her before. But now she was here. Present. Steady. SHE was here. “Good morning to you too” Agatha said smoothly, folding her hands over the table like she hadn’t just been ambushed. Her tone was mild. Icy. A performance. “I think I’m detecting a tone.”

    She was trying to be clever. To stay above it. But she was failing - because Rio wasn’t laughing. The heat coming off her was thick and furious.

    Agatha followed her gaze to the screen.

    * Ah. The contract. *

    Now it made sense. Rio had just received the email. The offer.

    The one inviting her - naming her - as the official showrunner of Lady Death. Agatha’s face remained serene. She leaned back in her chair with the same slow, effortless elegance that had disarmed studios and showrunners for years. Legs crossed. Chin lifted. A portrait of someone who had expected conflict - but had hoped for something a little more civilized.

    Yet there was a glint behind her eyes.

    Something Rio didn’t want to name but couldn’t quite ignore.

    A familiar softness.

    Something almost devotional, if you squinted past the toxicity.

    It was messed up.

    But it was real.

    Sweet, even - in the worst possible way.

    But Rio wasn’t in the mood for sentiment.

    It reminded her of those shared nights. Of laughter over beer and wine. Of Agatha acting like she actually gave a damn about creating something with her. Writing sessions that bled into dawn. Fingers laced on the kitchen table. Of kisses and false promises. It reminded her of the lies.

    “I don’t see the problem” the exec said, voice calm, almost amused. “Is there something wrong with the terms of the agreement?”

    “Bitch, you better be joking.”

    Agatha’s brow arched - not offended, just… puzzled. She couldn’t quite understand why things were escalating.

    “We agreed you’d be Lady Death’s showrunner” she said evenly “There’s no one better to defend it. To champion it.”

    Rio slammed her palms down on either side of the laptop.

    “We didn’t agree on shit.”

    She leaned in - slow and venomous - until her face hovered inches from Agatha’s. Her breath was short, her eyes blazing behind dark lenses. She bent lower, until they were level. The moment felt wrong in all the right ways.

    The reason?

    Agatha sat in the same chair where, once, she had straddled Rio - kissing her like she was starving, their lips, fingers, and breath tangled in something reckless and electric. A memory vivid enough to leave a scar.

    Its ghost lingered between them now.

    The Head Producer looked up at all that angry beauty as if cataloging the damage. She hadn’t seen Rio since the night everything fell apart - since it all exploded, collapsed, and began to rot. The night she’d killed whatever they had with one sharp-edged lie and a cruel smile she hadn’t even meant.

    It still pulsed in her brain like a hangover no amount of aspirin could cure. It wasn’t just avoidance that kept them apart - though that certainly played its part. Agatha had taken a few days off under the convenient excuse of helping Nicky settle into the house, easing into shared routines, hiding inside the comfort of the familiar. Playing the perfect mother.

    Pretending she was fine.

    And now Rio was here.

    Wrecked. Beautiful. Furious.

    Her gaze shifted to the sunglasses hiding Rio’s eyes.

    “You haven’t been sleeping” she pointed.

    Rio ripped the glasses off. Her eyes were bloodshot, rimmed in exhaustion. Not hate in them - but fire. Banked, restless fire with nowhere to go. “No shit” she muttered.

    Agatha saw it, then.

    The price of that night lingered in every red line beneath those breathtaking eyes. “You really need to sleep more” she said, gentler now.

    She knew Rio.

    They’d shared a bed enough times for Agatha to understand her rhythms - how she needed at least twelve hours to truly feel rested.

    She used to tease her for it, pretending not to know that the real reason her ex lover needed so much rest was the way their nights together used to unfold - savage, endless, consuming. Secretly she’d adored it and missed it.

    “I had too much on my mind” Rio muttered, lifting her hand to put the sunglasses back on. Agatha reached across the desk and closed her hand around Rio’s.

    She didn’t caress. Didn’t plead.

    She just held.

    For one second.

    Long enough to remember what it felt like to breathe in sync.

    She stopped her from putting the mask back on.

    And Rio didn’t pull away.

    For a moment, they just stood like that, trembling on the edge of something too big to name. Agatha cared about her. Profoundly.

    Now, finally, she knew it.

    She wanted to ask a thousand things.

    Was Rio eating? Was she high? Was she still writing?

    Did she - against all logic - still believe they had a shot at surviving this? But all that came out was: “What’s the problem with the contract? It’s exactly what we discussed“ Rio laughed. A harsh, joyless sound.

    “I’m telling you...we didn’t discuss anything, Agatha.”

    Agatha tried again, softer this time. Reaching for something that felt like grace. “Okay. Then let’s discuss it now.”

    If anyone could see how gentle she was being right now, they wouldn’t recognize her. She had never been anything but unyielding, and impossible to read within these four walls. “Please” she added, in a voice so soft, so painfully kind, it didn’t just feel out of place. It burned in Rio’s gut.

    Especially after the way that bitch had treated her just days ago - like she didn’t matter. Like she was nothing.

    Agatha’s hand hovered, almost reaching for Rio’s again, but she didn’t quite touch her. Not this time.

    She didn’t dare.

    “As you so unpolitely reminded me the other night” Rio said, stepping back like the desk was toxic, “you and I don’t need to discuss anything anymore.”

    Agatha’s voice dipped, low and careful. “Listen. I’m offering you an opportunity. A future. The one you deserve.”

    “Where’s Darcy’s name?”

    Agatha stilled, eyes narrowing in confusion. “Excuse me?”

    “Darcy” Rio clarified, enunciating every syllable like it physically hurt. “My writing partner. The person who co-created this fucking show with me. The one you’ve known about since day one.”

    The alluring woman in front of her furrowed a brow, her expression edged with concern. “What does she have to do with this?” she asked “I’m doing this for you.” Rio stared at her, genuinely stunned.

    “You’re shitting me, right?” Her voice rising like thunder about to crack open the sky “You actually think handing me a solo showrunner credit after treating me like garbage is some grand act of loyalty?”

    There was no guilt in Agatha's eyes. Just confusion.

    “I know you hate me, but...”

    “I don’t hate you, Agatha” Rio’s voice sliced through the air “God. You’re such a narcissist. You really can’t see it, can you?”

    She waited - for anything.

    A flicker of remorse. A step back. A human moment.

    But nothing came.

    “This is wrong” she explained, pointing to the screen like it was radioactive. “Fix it.” Agatha’s face hardened. It changed almost imperceptibly - just a shift in the eyes, in the set of her jaw - but it was enough. The warmth drained from the room.

    She was caught off guard - unsteady beneath the surface - but she’d never admit it. Not even to herself.

    And beneath that? Fear.

    Real, raw fear that Rio was slipping through her fingers - and fast.

    So the Reaper slid into place like a second skin.

    “What, exactly, do I need to fix?” she asked coolly, tilting her head just a little. “You have talent. She doesn’t. End of story.”

    Rio flinched.

    Visibly.

    Like Agatha had slapped her across the face.

    Her voice cracked as she replied. “Don’t do this. Just... don’t. Not again. I want to have at least one good memory left.”

    Agatha stood. Slowly.

    The chair whispered against the polished floor as she rose. One hand touched the table - reflexive, grounding.

    She moved with elegance, yes, but it wasn’t performative. It was practiced restraint. Years of learning how to weaponize poise.

    She circled the table - closer to Rio now, though she didn’t reach for her. Her hands lifted, palms forward, like she was showing she had nothing to hide. Not surrender. Not quite. But maybe the closest she’d ever get to it.

    The Reaper was there - always. Laced into her bones. But this wasn’t a mask. This was just Agatha.

    Unarmored.

    Not entirely, but enough.

    Her shoulders were loose.

    Her voice dropped to something private, low, intimate. The kind of tone she only ever used early in the morning - when everything still smelled like sleep and skin and safety. The same voice that made Rio freeze, ache, remember.

    This was the Agatha who used to knelt on a vintage rug with a glass of red wine in one hand and her mouth between her thighs. The one who whispered, 'You’re good, you know that?' after reading her first draft out loud, underlining every sentence with her fingertips. Who laughed at the dumbest jokes like they were little miracles. The woman Rio had helplessly fallen for.

    “Don’t you see?” Her perfect mistake said now, softer than she had any right to be. “I’m giving you the opportunity of a lifetime.”

    “Well, I don’t want it” Rio replied, voice raw and trembling, held together by nothing but heartbreak and leftover pride. “I don’t want anything from you. I don’t even want to be in this fucking room right now.”

    She stepped back, one pace, then another, as if trying to create space not just physically but existentially. As if the distance might offer some kind of clarity.

    “I’m so sick of your games. Your back-and-forth. Your...” Her voice broke, the sentence unfinished, swallowed by everything she couldn't say without unraveling completely. Her throat caught. Her breath hitched. The heat in her chest surged into her jaw, then her eyes, and she blinked it back - rage, pain - refusing to let any of it fall down her cheeks. “I just want to breathe.”

    The silence that followed wasn’t empty - it was heavy. Dense with everything left unsaid. With heat, and history, and heartbreak. It pressed in, thick with sleepless nights, backhanded accusations, and calls that never came. With every orgasm that had tasted like love, every morning that had felt like a lie, and the bitter aftertaste of broken trust. “Please, just... let me breathe” she continued, this time pleading. “I get it. You don’t love me. That’s okay. I let myself believe in something that wasn’t real. But this...” she gestured at the laptop, at the cursor blinking like a heartbeat she couldn’t resuscitate “this is wrong. And you know it.”

    Another beat of silence. The cursor blinked again. And again. Like a countdown. Agatha didn’t speak at first. She had nothing clever to say. No retort. She just stood there, watching Rio, and in that stillness, something inside her fractured.

    She looked smaller now. Not diminished - just human. As if for once she was letting herself be seen instead of managing the angles of how she was perceived.

    She opened her mouth, but no sound came. Then, finally, the words broke loose, rough and unscripted: “I’m… I’m sorry.”

    It wasn’t performative. It wasn’t calculated. It was the kind of sorry that tasted bitter going down. The kind she’d never said to anyone and barely believed she was saying now. She remembered every word she said in that kitchen. Every fucking syllable. She remembered the way she’d twisted the knife and smiled while doing it, convincing herself it was mercy. That it was necessary.

    “I completely lost the plot.”

    She wanted to move. To close the distance between them. To gather Rio into her arms and hold her, press her against her chest and feel the weight of her. To comfort her - for everything she'd had put her through, for everything she’d failed to be. But she didn’t.

    She stayed rooted to the spot, just watching Rio - waiting for her to speak, to move, to do anything. She watched her struggle to keep it together, breathing through her nose like she was trying not to scream. Saw the way her shoulders tensed, still reeling from the shock of what had just come out of her mouth.

    This was unexpected. For Rio, at least.

    Not for Agatha.

    She’d had days to think. Days in her home office, surrounded by the quiet hum of her carefully constructed life. Hours of sitting in that leather chair, staring out the windows, trying to make sense of why Rio’s absence felt less like a missing piece and more like the collapse of the entire structure.

    And all the while, the purple lily Rio had given her had stayed right where she’d treasured it - in its little ceramic pot, untouched, just behind her desk. Watching her back. She’d spent hours staring at that flower.

    Wondering.

    How could someone who saw her so clearly - who knew her better than she sometimes knew herself - still have hope for her? Still believe there was something worth loving under all that armor?

    Her home had been full lately. Her son’s laughter echoing down the hall. The bunny hopping from room to room like it owned the place. The rhythm of a life that was close to perfect. And in that fullness, that deceptive peace, the truth had landed: This was her life. Her rules.

    She could change them.

    She could reach for someone, if she wanted to. She could dream, if she dared. The fog had lifted.

    That was when she saw it: how different versions of herself had always surfaced around different people.

    She used to think that meant she was manipulative. But now… now she wondered if maybe it just meant she had range.

    That there were rooms inside her she hadn’t even entered yet.

    And each person unlocked a new door.

    But with Rio?

    With her, all the doors stayed open.

    The chaos. The ambition. The hunger. The fear.

    Rio had seen it all. Taken it all. Carried it, even, like it wasn’t a burden but a privilege. Who would throw away someone like that?

    Only a fool.

    And for the first time in her life, Agatha Harkness felt a strange kind of pride. Quiet. Painful. But real. Solid.

    Because maybe - just maybe - she wasn’t that fool anymore.

    Maybe she’d finally figured something out and this was the beginning of something different. Something better.

    Maybe this was what bravery actually looked like.

    Not control. Not dominance. Not silence.

    Just saying she was sorry.

    And meaning it with her whole goddamn soul.

    Rio’s voice broke the tension.

    “Why are you saying that now?”

    Agatha blinked.

    Rio stepped closer. Not much. Just enough to keep the heat between them simmering. “What are you apologizing for, Agatha? Be specific.”

    Her expression unreadable. There was no hatred there. Only a weariness that struck deeper. Agatha stared at her, thrown.

    “For the way I spoke to you.”

    Rio’s eyes narrowed slightly. Her mouth twisted - not cruelly, but with a grief that felt older than either of them.

    “What else?”

    Agatha just looked at her. Didn’t answer.

    “See?” Rio said, shaking her head. “That’s the problem. You don’t think there’s anything else.”

    “But...”

    “You said some pretty fucking ugly things to me. Awful things. And I almost believed you. I almost believed I meant nothing to you. Because you were so damn convincing.” Rio’s voice didn’t crack, but it carried weight - something old and raw. “But then I realized... that’s your real talent, isn’t it?” she went on. “You lie. You perform like you’re telling the truth. And sometimes the lies are so good no one knows what’s real anymore. Not even you.”

    Agatha tried to speak - tried to defend herself, or at least explain. She was shaken by how precisely Rio saw her. And somehow, deep beneath the shame, there was a flicker of relief. Someone had finally read her right.

    “Let me finish.” Her could-have-been stopped her, holding up a hand.

    “Words are one thing. But your actions? How could I not believe your actions? she continued, voice flat now, bitter. “You held me like I was something sacred... and then lived like I didn’t exist. That’s when shit gets complicated. Cause that’s the part that’s real. The part I can’t un-feel .”

    Agatha swallowed hard and stepped forward, just slightly. “I said I’m sorry. I mean it. I’m sorry for everything.”

    Rio nodded.

    “I understand” she said. “And I accept your apology.”

    Agatha’s breath caught. Her heart stumbled, hopeful for half a second. “I just...” Rio exhaled. Her expression shifted - something fragile sparking across her face before it vanished again. “I won’t forgive you. Obviously.”

    Her backstaber's eyes widened. Desperation bled through. She moved to step closer, but Rio mirrored the motion - backward. The distance held.

    "What can I do to fix this?" Agatha asked.

    No one could really blame her for asking. She wasn’t used to this kind of grief, or this kind of closeness. In so many ways, she was still socially clumsy. She just happened to wear it better than most.

    Rio’s smile was the saddest thing Agatha had ever seen. It held no cruelty, no edge. Only exhaustion. And underneath that, the ghost of something else - affection, maybe. Or the ruins of it.

    She shook her head slowly, like someone who still had the knife lodged in her chest and no strength left to pull it out.

    Agatha nodded in response. Once. Small. Accepting. She didn’t press.

    And somewhere in that silence - somewhere in the heavy space between them - the air changed. It thickened. Turned sacred. Or dangerous. Maybe both.

    Who would’ve thought, all those months ago, that Agatha Harkness would tie her fate to a broke, gutter-born screenwriter with ink-stained fingers and a defiant mouth? That she’d fuck her into delirium, again and again, until Rio couldn’t fall asleep without the imprint of Agatha’s teeth on her skin?

    That in return, she wouldn’t just let Rio leave marks on her body - but somewhere deeper? That she’d hand over her heart - raw, bloody, still beating - and let Rio crush it right in front of her?

    Circling back to the reason she’d come upstairs in the first place, the writer crossed her arms tightly over her chest. Her voice turned flat. Unsentimental. Final.

    “I’m not taking the showrunner position, Agatha.”

    The producer turned away at once, giving the other woman her back - shielding her face before it could betray her.

    She fixed her gaze on the floor-to-ceiling window, like she might somehow vanish into the skyline.

    The city of dreams stretched out before her - sun-bleached and endless, a sprawl of palm trees, hazy hills, and glittering freeways snaking through it all like arteries. The light had that particular glow that only LA could pull off. It grounded her. Just enough to hold her posture steady, to keep her hands from shaking and to mask the raw sting burning in her chest. “You should. It’s yours” she said evenly. “It’s already been arranged and it’s the only way you’ll have full control over your work. All you have to do is say yes.” * And it gives us a reason to keep seeing each other. *

    “As we’ve already established” Rio replied “I’m not taking that title without Darcy. I’m not cutting her out just to sit at your fucking table.”

    Agatha’s hands curled into fists at her sides. She didn’t turn.

    The rejection landed hard - deeper than she wanted to admit.

    It sliced through the carefully constructed logic. Through the professionalism. Through the defense mechanisms.

    The hurt twisted, then curdled.

    And this time, when the Reaper rose in full power - cold, composed, calculating - Agatha didn’t stop her.

    It was easier that way.

    “I refuse to give you more special treatment, Vidal” she said, like her almost-girlfriend name was an inconvenience.

    Rio’s spine snapped straight. “Excuse me?”

    “You heard me.”

    “Yeah, I heard you just fine. Do you hear yourself?” Her hands were at her hairline now, pulling her hair back in disbelief.

    “I’m honoring our deal” Agatha said. Her voice was low, almost a growl. “You’re the one trying to twist it.”

    “I’m the one twis....!?” the girl's laugh was sharp this time. Wounded “You don’t even see it, do you? You actually think you’re being generous. You think I should be grateful for whatever crumbs you’re throwing, when everything, the tone, the characters, the fucking world, was built on me and Darcy bleeding into those pages.”

    “She doesn’t want the spotlight” Agatha said.

    “That’s not true, and you know it.”

    “She doesn’t deserve it.”

    Rio took another step forward. Her voice was trembling, but it didn’t waver. “That’s also not true. And again, you know it.”

    Agatha shrugged, but there was something cruel in the tilt of her mouth. “Maybe I should’ve fucked her instead. Might’ve made all this simpler.”

    The words landed like glass breaking across the floor.

    Rio stood there for half a second, stunned. Then she exhaled slowly.

    “Why do you always do this?” she asked, voice low, tight. “Why do you go from zero to destruction in ten seconds flat?”

    Agatha turned toward her fully now - only to realize how close her ex lover had gotten. There were inches between them.

    “Do you really think Darcy would’ve tried to leverage sex for power?” Agatha asked. Her tone was part scorn, part dare. “Do you think she would’ve tried to get you a seat at the table?”

    Rio’s mouth twitched, not quite a smile. “Do you honestly believe that’s what I’m doing? That I’m using you?”

    “Aren’t you?”

    And that was it.

    “You know what?” Rio said. “I’m out. You...this job....this whole glass fucking castle....it’s not for me. I don’t want anything with your name on it. Fuck you, Harkness. And fuck your job offer”.

    “You can’t just walk away” Agatha remarked, her voice clipped and cold - Reaper mode fully engaged now. “You’re under contract as a staff writer. You know it.”

    Her not-so-old bedmade froze at the door, one hand on the knob.

    She didn’t turn.

    “I don’t bow to anyone, Agatha” she replied. “As I said...fuck the contract.” She twisted the knob.

    But Agatha’s voice stopped her cold once more.

    “If you walk away now, your friend walks with you.”

    Rio turned. Slowly.

    Agatha held her ground, gaze unblinking. “I’ll drop Lewis.”

    Rio’s reaction was immediate - violent, visceral. “You didn’t just say that.” The silence that followed was loud enough to scream.

    Her toxic obsession stood taller, a shadow of danger laced through her stillness. When she spoke again, her voice was softer, but no less brutal.

    “I can’t afford to let you spiral and drag the whole project down with you. If you go rogue, the board will start asking questions. It’s easier if the break is clean.” Rio stared at her like she didn’t recognize the woman standing there. Like she couldn’t believe how fast everything had rotted.

    “Are you seriously threatening her because of me?” Her voice cracked with disbelief. Fury. Pain.

    “I’m protecting the show.” Agatha stated, icy and immovable.

    “The show?” Rio shot back, her voice rising, raw. “Or your ego?”

    “I’m just doing what needs to be done.”

    “No” the desperate writer spat, shaking. “You’re blackmailing me with my best friend’s career.”

    “She’s in because of you” Agatha said sharply. “This was always your deal. If you break it, it collapses.”

    “No” Rio said again, quieter this time, dead in the eyes. “If it breaks, it’s because you broke it.”

    Agatha moved closer. Not threatening. Just...there. Present. Her gaze didn’t leave Rio’s face. “I want you on this project” she insisted softly. “Not because of anything between us. Because you’re brilliant. Because the work is better with you and you see things I don’t. This isn’t personal.”

    Rio’s laugh was guttural. Bitter.

    “Of course it’s personal” she said. “That’s the fucking problem.”

    Her employer looked at her - really looked. And for the first time, she saw herself reflected back: a woman who had taken and taken and convinced herself it was generosity. Who had used the language of love to mask control. Who had ruined what could have been extraordinary.

    “Please” she uttered, almost whispering now. “Please, don’t go.”

    “You don’t get to ask that” Rio replied. Her voice was trembling. “Not after everything.” “Why not?”

    Rio’s mouth fell open in disbelief. “Are you seriously playing clueless right now?” She stepped in again. Dangerously close. Fury radiated off her like heat from asphalt in July. She wasn’t angry - she was seismic.

    “You do realize there are actual human beings with actual lives in the background of your drama, right?” she asked, voice vibrating. “You’re playing god with people's futures, Agatha.”

    “That’s life.” The producer said flatly, like she'd just dropped a final card on the table. “No” Rio snapped, stepping forward so fast the air between them vanished. Her face was suddenly inches away, eyes blazing. She jabbed a finger – hard - against Agatha’s chest. “That’s you being an asshole.”

    The contact didn’t hurt. Not really. But the accusation landed like a strike to the sternum. The exec blinked, momentarily thrown off balance. She wasn’t used to being checked like that.

    Certainly not by this girl.

    And definitely not like this.

    This version of Rio was... new. Volatile. There was nothing soft or apologetic in her. It wasn’t the heat that unsettled the Pitch Killer - it was the clarity. The control. Something primal stirred under her skin in response. Something unwelcome and thrilling. She narrowed her eyes, more intrigued than insulted.

    “This is new” she murmured, raising one lazy hand to trace a slow, invisible line from Rio’s forehead to her toes. Not touching - just close enough to let the heat of her presence register. “What is this?”

    She wasn’t talking about the argument.

    She was talking about the posture.

    The dominance.

    The threat.
